papers.title: Bayesian inference with a polymer probabilistic computer
papers.abstract: Bayesian inference weighs competing explanations of noisy data by sampling from a posterior distribution, a task that deterministic hardware performs only by simulating randomness. Probabilistic bits (p-bits) supply this randomness physically, but the few hardware networks of p-bits built so far use inorganic devices, address optimization or learning, and are judged without reference to the spread expected from finite sampling. Here we report a probabilistic computer built from solution-processed conjugated-polymer memristors. Four polymer p-bits, tracked online for drift and coupled in a closed Gibbs-sampling loop, sample competing, degenerate and cooperative posteriors over sixteen states with statistics that fall within the range of ideal p-bits, both in their distribution and in their autocorrelation, without any parameter fitted to the target. This agreement extends to new simulated sensor readings whose outcome was predicted before each run, including readings that point away from the true answer. Reprogrammed in software, the same circuit and controller reproduces the invertible AND gate of earlier p-bit networks, with its temperature fixed in advance rather than fitted. Polymer p-bits thus open a route to printed, large-area probabilistic computers that infer alongside their sensors.

papers.title: Digitally Supported Transitional Care Pathways for Older Adults: A Multi-Site Co-Design Study
papers.abstract: During transitions from hospital to home, older adults are frequently affected by fragmented communication, limited coordination between levels of care, and insufficient post-discharge follow-up. Digital technologies, including remote patient monitoring (RPM), digital communication, and artificial intelligence (AI), offer opportunities to improve continuity of care. However, their integration needs to reflect the organizational and clinical contexts of different healthcare systems. This study presents the development and early implementation of digitally supported transitional care pathways within the TransCare project. Care pathways were analyzed and redesigned across three pilot sites in Italy, Romania, and Norway. Existing clinical and organizational processes were mapped to identify challenges and opportunities for improvement. Technology-augmented pathway matrices were developed to integrate RPM, digital communication tools, and AI-supported analytics across the stages of assessment, hospitalization, discharge, and post-discharge follow-up. The pathways were iteratively refined through a co-design process involving healthcare professionals, patients, caregivers, and technical partners. Early implementation experiences were subsequently analyzed across the three sites. Common challenges included fragmented communication and poor care coordination, particularly during discharge and post-discharge follow-up. However, the underlying cause and required solutions differed across the pilot sites, reflecting variations in patient profiles, healthcare organizations, available resources, and digital maturity.

papers.title: Beyond Ground States: Learning Many-Body Hamiltonians for p-Bit Invertible Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Probabilistic-bit (p-bit) invertible logic encodes a Boolean relation as an energy whose ground states are its legal assignments, computing in any direction by sampling. Traditional constructions target ground-state membership and a wide minimum energy gap, yet finite-time samplers traverse excited states. We cast Hamiltonian design as inverse statistical mechanics: fit an energy with interactions up to order four whose Gibbs law approaches uniformity on each clamp case's legal states, under a gap floor keeping every legal state below every illegal one. Constrained maximum likelihood with pruning and refitting fits terms from a fixed pool, and every delivered energy is audited exactly on all cases. Each energy is scored by time to a verified solution under restarts with its best of nine tuned samplers. In underdetermined modes, learned multipliers factor in 0.55, 0.44, 0.52 and 0.46 [0.38, 0.56] of the hand-written encodings' updates from 4x4 to 7x7, faster within every family below 7x7 at no resolved work penalty; learned adders solve the reverse mode in 0.71 of the updates at 8 bits and about a quarter at 24 and 32 bits, at 0.55 of the work at 32 bits. At 5x5 under equal pool, budget and floor, a gap-maximizing fit reaches 0.79 [0.73, 0.88] in updates and 1.26 in work against the hand-written encoding, while likelihood fitting takes 0.55 [0.46, 0.58] and 0.58 [0.48, 0.61] of the gap fit's updates and work. Rounding coefficients to the narrowest exact integer words tested, we run both energies at each pair's common word on one FPGA color-sweep SSA core, bit-exact with software: learned multipliers take 0.41 of the hand-written encoding's cycles at 4x4 and 0.057 [0.045, 0.068] at 7x7, at up to 2.4 times its lookup tables. The method requires only a circuit's legal assignments; in determined modes, hand-written encodings take less work, and from 12 bits on the adder fewer updates.

papers.title: Hybrid Classical-Quantum Optimization for CVRPTW: A Systems Framework with Provable Feasibility and Empirical Hardware Limits
papers.abstract: Solving large-scale Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problems with Time Windows (CVRPTW) remains challenging because strict operational constraints and scale limit both exact and heuristic methods. We present a hybrid classical-quantum architecture combining Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) with vehicle-level Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO), solved using Toshiba SQBM+ and QAOA on Rigetti Ankaa-3 and IQM Emerald quantum processors. The decomposition avoids the variable growth and constraint-enforcement difficulties of monolithic CVRPTW QUBO formulations. We evaluate the framework on five realistic benchmarks derived from London traffic and location data, spanning 10--70 customers, using a validation pipeline enforcing feasibility and monotone improvement over classical baselines. SQBM+ achieves verified fleet-distance reductions of 2.80% (7,927 m) for the 25-customer instance and 0.22% (1,186 m) for the 55-customer instance. QAOA experiments establish a current hardware boundary for reliable constraint satisfaction at subproblems of up to 4 customers (16 qubits). Diagnostic results identify assignment-level time-window tightness, rather than local route optimization, as the dominant scalability bottleneck. The results demonstrate a practical near-term role for hybrid classical-quantum optimization while establishing empirical limits for current quantum hardware.

papers.title: TGen-SQD: Physics-Informed Transferable Configuration Generator for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) avoids iterative variational circuit optimization, but its accuracy and cost depend on selecting a compact determinant subspace that captures the ground state. Existing machine-learning selectors use task-specific physical cues and typically retrain for each Hamiltonian. We introduce TGen-SQD, a physics-informed generator jointly trained across multiple Hamiltonians. It learns from configuration-interaction-weighted data and uses orbital- and system-level descriptors to guide generation. After training, its weights remain frozen for inference on seen and zero-shot geometries. On a 20-qubit H10 chain, TGen-SQD achieves mean energy errors of 40.18 +/- 1.52 and 43.97 +/- 1.20 mHa on seen and unseen geometries, respectively, 12.7% and 11.7% lower than the state-of-the-art PIGen-SQD baseline under matched shot and proposal budgets.

papers.title: Hierarchical Decoding for Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders that can keep up with syndrome data streams and supply correction information and logical measurement outcomes to the quantum control system. Meeting these requirements at scale requires high throughput while controlling the end-to-end latency from readout to usable correction. In this paper, we organize decoding algorithms, execution strategies, and code constructions using common classifications and examine their performance and trade-offs under the reported evaluation conditions. We distinguish decoder-level hierarchy, where multiple decoding stages or resources cooperate to decode a single code, from code-level hierarchy, where the code construction itself introduces multiple decoding levels. We first review single-code hierarchical decoders and their cascaded predecoding and windowed, streaming, and distributed implementations. We then study hierarchical and concatenated codes, focusing on how decoding is coordinated across code levels through hard decisions, soft reliability information, or syndrome information. We also examine how qubit modalities shape decoding workloads and timing requirements, and review how different decoding platforms meet these requirements, including central processing units (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), and cryogenic platforms. By assessing design trade-offs, this paper clarifies connections across the literature and provides a shared foundation for QEC design exploration. It also identifies gaps in performance reporting and system integration to guide future research toward practical quantum error correction.

papers.title: Demo: Matter-Based IoMT Telemetry and Security Analysis
papers.abstract: Connected health devices increasingly support health monitoring outside clinical settings, making secure and accessible physiological data important for patients and caregivers. However, device-specific applications and interfaces complicate the integration of readings from different devices. The Matter standard provides standardized device commissioning and protected communication, but its cluster library does not represent the health attribute measurement. We present a preliminary demo study of a Matter-based IoMT testbed with a specific HealthVitals cluster. Implemented in the connectedhomeip SDK on a Raspberry~Pi~5, the cluster exposes simulated heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, and body temperature. We examine commissioning, attribute retrieval, communication under simulated packet loss, and operational traffic through a reference controller. The study demonstrates that this custom telemetry model can operate within the tested Matter configuration without modifying commissioning or secure-session mechanisms. The resulting testbed gives researchers and device developers a concrete platform for investigating health-oriented extensions. It also supports exploration of local telemetry integration that could help patients and caregivers access readings across connected devices.

papers.title: Scaling Pêlagos: Multi-GPU Orchestration for Relay Belief-Propagation Decoding
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum error-correction (QEC) decoders that achieve low logical error rates under real-time operating constraints. These constraints motivate heuristic decoding algorithms whose error-correction performance must be evaluated through large-scale simulation. High-throughput decoding accelerates this evaluation and the exploration of decoder parameters. Using multiple graphics processing units (GPUs) is a natural way to scale these simulations, but naively distributing syndrome batches introduces host-side preprocessing and output-collection overheads that limit scaling. To address these limitations, we extend the P\^elagos relay belief-propagation (Relay-BP) decoder with process-isolated orchestration, parallel host preprocessing, and shared-memory output. We evaluate both one-gross ($[[144,12,12]]$) and two-gross ($[[288,12,18]]$) codes in a multi-GPU environment. Specifically, for the one-gross circuit at $R=50$, eight AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs and eight AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs achieve optimized end-to-end speedups of $5.68\times$ and $6.23\times$, respectively. For the two-gross circuit, the corresponding speedups are $6.92\times$ and $7.01\times$. When throughput is calculated using GPU decoding time, the corresponding two-gross speedups are $7.58\times$ and $7.45\times$, indicating near-linear GPU scaling. We deploy P\^elagos on Lux, Oak Ridge National Laboratory's AMD Instinct MI355X-based supercomputer, as a pathfinding application for high-throughput QEC simulation. This deployment provides a concrete quantum-computing use case for the AI + HPC infrastructure supporting the Genesis Mission's scientific-discovery goals. These end-to-end measurements demonstrate a practical path to accelerating large-scale QEC simulation through efficient multi-GPU decoding.

papers.title: A Joint LLM and Optimization Agent Solution for Drone Scheduling in Victim Search Missions
papers.abstract: Victim search in wilderness areas is time-critical. Drones enable rapid area search, but scheduling them is challenging because victims may continue moving, detection results are uncertain, and effective decisions must combine structured mission information with unstructured contextual clues and domain knowledge. To address this, we propose an agent-aided drone scheduling system. The system employs an agent at the ground control station (GCS) to coordinate multiple drones over successive search cycles. In each cycle, the agent applies a scheduling policy that combines a large language model (LLM) for reasoning about where to search with an optimizer for determining how to dispatch the drones under energy constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed system consistently completes the victim-search mission, whereas none of the six non-LLM baselines does so and direct LLM scheduling is considerably less reliable. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/1643204431/llm-uav-victim-search.

papers.title: Exploring Socially Acceptable 3D Feedback Design for Inclusive Small-Group Conversation
papers.abstract: Prior research has shown that providing feedback on group dynamics can improve the quality of small-group conversations. However, publicly delivered feedback that targets specific individuals may reduce social acceptability due to negative experiences such as social pressure, embarrassment, and resistance. This work investigates how public feedback can be designed to remain socially acceptable while maintaining its effectiveness in XR-based small-group conversations. Informed by social science and HCI literature, we identified three design strategies (incorporate humor, reduce social attention, and use indirectness) and proposed a set of metaphor- and agent-based 3D feedback probes. We then conducted a two-phase study: (1) an online survey with 50 participants to examine how such feedback designs are perceived under public and private delivery, and (2) follow-up interviews with 14 participants who completed the survey to better understand their interpretations and elicit additional insights. Results show that metaphor- and agent-based feedback can reduce social discomfort while maintaining effectiveness. Interview findings further highlighted the role of three strategies in making feedback easier to accept, while requiring careful balance. We also discussed design implications for creating socially acceptable 3D feedback to support inclusive small-group conversations in XR.

papers.title: Broadcast, Don't Replicate: Eliminating Weight HBM in Datacenter LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference at datacenter scale is fundamentally bottlenecked by memory capacity and bandwidth limits. Because model weights are read-only and identical across instances, conventional architectures that replicate these parameters across the local DRAM of tens of thousands of accelerators incur massive capital expenditures, significant static power dissipation, and redundant memory-fetch energy. A recent proposal to use optical fiber loops as delay-line memory alleviates these issues, but its recirculating loop must hold the whole model: loop length grows with model size, slack is fixed when the ring is built, and the layouts that serve modern Mixture of Experts (MoE) models efficiently do not fit in it. We propose Optical Broadcast Memory (OBM), an open-ended hierarchical Tap-and-Amplify fiber architecture that generalizes and replaces the optical ring paradigm. A centralized memory server continuously broadcasts weights to distributed inference nodes that passively tap the data stream using receive-only co-packaged optics, delivering parameters directly to compute units without intermediate buffering. To overcome the limitations of continuous weight streaming, we use dynamically-sized slack to accommodate large and variable context lengths. We show how removing the restrictions of the optical ring allows OBM to efficiently serve MoE models. Evaluated at a datacenter scale of 80,000 accelerators, OBM eliminates petabytes of HBM while being competitive or better in throughput and energy per token than an HBM-based system.

papers.title: Augmented Hybrid TV Services. Habits, Preferences, Opinions and Expectations of Spanish Consumers
papers.abstract: The convergence of hybrid broadcast and broadband delivery, companion devices, and immersive technologies enables new forms of interactive, personalized, and accessible TV services. This paper introduces the concept of Augmented Hybrid TV services and presents an exploratory user requirements and preliminary acceptance assessment for 5 representative use cases. They were selected through an exploratory stakeholder consultation and 3 co-design workshops with audiovisual professionals and participants from organizations supporting people with visual or hearing impairments. They combine conventional TV with complementary content delivered to connected devices, including AR/VR HMD. They were subsequently evaluated through a cross-sectional CAWI survey of 626 Internet and connected TV users in Spain. Each participant viewed standardized video demonstrations of 2 randomly assigned cases and assessed their perceived usefulness, anticipated benefits/limitations, and interest in them. The results show substantial interest across all five use cases, ranging from 64.7% to 76.9%. Adaptive and personalized augmented subtitles received the highest level of interest and were particularly valued for their accessibility, language-learning, and personalization benefits. Immersive services involving complementary AR content, virtual screens, 3D objects, and 360 video were also evaluated positively, although participants identified device cost, ergonomics, connectivity, usability, and synchronization as anticipated limitations. The findings provide user-centered evidence that can inform the prioritization, design, and subsequent prototype-based evaluation of standards-compliant Augmented Hybrid TV services. Because the study assessed video-based scenarios rather than functional systems, the results represent perceived usefulness and stated interest rather than observed adoption or technically validated QoE.
